deck: SCREEN, ASSIGN, LOCATE ASSETS, AND ENFORCE THE 80 PERCENT OF JUDGMENTS COURTS NEVER COLLECT
GARNISHMENTS, LEVIES, LIENS, DEBTOR EXAMS, AND COMPLIANCE GATES BUILT INTO CONTINGENCY DEAL FLOW
site_ui.lead: Courts award money but never enforce it, so the practitioners in these 12 chapters take assignment of unpaid judgments, front enforcement costs, locate bank accounts, wages, and property, and keep one-third to one-half of what they collect.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies covering the judgment recovery business, from assignments and debtor examinations to garnishments, liens, out-of-state domestication, bankruptcy, FDCPA and Regulation F risk, and judgment lifespan. Every claim, metric, pro-tip, and operator gate carries timestamped inline attribution to the practitioner channel and video it came from.

flow: Check bankruptcy filings and death records first, then rate each judgment on where the debtor moved, its size, and other judgments, refusing the roughly 30 percent rated uncollectible
Convert the creditor's judgment into a notarized assignment on a 50/50 contingency split or cash purchase, and do not start collecting until it is filed and returned by the court
Confirm an attachable asset exists before signing, locating bank accounts first and sending notices only to debtors with a verified asset
Pursue driver's license suspension, bank garnishment, wage garnishment of up to 25 percent of gross pay, liens, and till taps
Trade writ dismissal for $500 down plus $100 to $200 a month, building a payment stream of about $3,000 per month by the third month
File SC-130, SC-290, or EJ-100 on full payment without letting a debtor's written demand sit 14 days, and re-check dead files about six months later
